title: Korea Stock Market Today, Oct 21, 2026: KOSPI +3.29%, KOSDAQ +1.38% as Elice Hits Limit-Up
content:
KOSPI closed at 5,735.66, up 3.29%, and KOSDAQ closed at 792.76, up 1.38%, as dip buying lifted both indexes the day after a sharp drop; a buy-side sidecar was triggered on KOSPI during the session. Individual themes moved on their own news: AI neocloud company Elice hitting its daily upper limit, Taihan Fiber Optics' second U.S. data center cable order, Tesla and SpaceX merger talks, and record October semiconductor exports.

1. Rebound after the plunge — KOSPI and KOSDAQ rise together

KOSPI rose 3.29% from the previous session to 5,735.66 and KOSDAQ rose 1.38% to 792.76. Bargain buying after the prior day's sharp fall lifted both markets, and buying on KOSPI was strong enough to trigger a buy-side sidecar during the session.

2. Elice hits its upper limit — AI-related stocks strengthen

AI infrastructure company Elice rebounded after a sharp fall on its first trading day and jumped 29.92% to 79,900 won, hitting the daily upper limit. Expectations for growth in AI computing infrastructure and cloud business stood out, and reports said its first-half revenue was about three times the level of a year earlier. Polaris AI and Flitto also drew attention in the theme. Others mentioned were NHN, iCraft, GNC Energy (data center power and facilities) and Seohan (data center construction hopes). Investment expectations for AI data centers and computing spread across related stocks, but business links and actual AI revenue share differ by company, so direct beneficiaries should be separated out.

3. Taihan Fiber Optics supplies cable to a U.S. AI data center — optical communication stocks in focus

Taihan Fiber Optics drew attention after a second order of optical cable for a U.S. hyperscale AI data center. The second contract is worth about 35.5 billion won, bringing the total with the first contract to about 41.1 billion won. The cable is a 864-fiber ultra-high-count type for North American data centers, and expectations rose for network infrastructure that moves large amounts of data. Other names in focus included RN2 Technology, Bitsaem Electronics and DASAN Networks, along with Gaon Cable, LS Eco Energy and OE Solutions. The contract belongs to Taihan Fiber Optics, and direct orders for the other stocks should be checked separately.

4. Elice's limit-up lifts newly listed stocks

Elice's upper-limit move on its second trading day increased interest in newly listed and recently listed stocks. Short-term buying flowed into volatile early-listing names such as Lemonhealthcare, Bigwave Robotics and Melcon. Newly listed stocks can swing widely with tradable share supply and early order flow, so post-listing supply and demand matters alongside a company's earnings and business.

5. Tesla and SpaceX merger talks — space stocks in focus

Elon Musk expressed a positive view on merging Tesla and SpaceX, and news said the two companies formed a special committee to review a possible merger. This is still at the discussion stage; no terms or final merger have been confirmed. LK Samyang, Vitzro NexTech, Kencoa Aerospace and Naraspace Technology drew attention as space-themed stocks, and Satrec Initiative, Intellian Technologies, Innospace and Hanwha Systems were also mentioned. The merger talks do not mean direct orders or earnings gains for Korean space companies.

6. Record semiconductor exports for Oct 1–20 — chip equipment and materials strengthen

Korea Customs Service data showed preliminary exports for October 1–20 of $61.6 billion, up 105.4% from a year earlier. Semiconductor exports were $27.5 billion, up 222.5%, the highest for the same period in any October. Rising chip demand from AI data center investment was cited. Super Micro Computer earnings expectations and news that Musk is moving up equipment delivery schedules from suppliers such as ASML for his Terafab project added to interest, with full-scale chip production targeted for the second half of 2028. Names in focus included Chemtros, Komico and Hana Materials (materials and parts); KC Tech, Zeus and Dawon Nexview (equipment); Mirae Corporation and SFA Semicon (test and back-end); and Hanyang Digitech and Fidelix (memory and design). HPSP, Hanmi Semiconductor and Unicem were also mentioned. Whether each company is actually in the Terafab supply chain differs, so names without a confirmed supply contract are better read as expectation-driven theme moves.

Quick FAQ

Why did KOSPI rise on Oct 21?
Bargain buying after the previous day's sharp drop lifted KOSPI to 5,735.66 (+3.29%) and KOSDAQ to 792.76 (+1.38%), and a buy-side sidecar was triggered on KOSPI.

How much did Elice rise?
It rose 29.92% to 79,900 won and hit the daily upper limit after a sharp fall on its first trading day.

Is the Tesla and SpaceX merger confirmed?
No. A special committee was reported to be formed to review a merger; terms and a final deal are not confirmed.
